n: All the military leaders, including Johanan and Jezaniah, and all the people, from least to greatest, approached Jeremiah.

f.g: Probably the same as “Azariah son of Hoshaiah” in 43:2.

n: They humbly ask him to pray to “the Lord your God” for them, since only a small remnant is left. Notice: “your God”—not yet “our God.”

f.w: we are left but a few of many

n: They ask God to show them which way to go and what to do. It sounds sincere—but their minds were already largely made up (41:17).
Jeremiah agrees to pray to “the Lord your God,” gently reminding them that God is theirs too, and promises to tell them everything God says, holding nothing back.

f.w: I will keep nothing back from you

n: They swear an oath: may the Lord be a true witness against us if we don’t do everything he tells us.
“Whether we like the answer or not, we will obey the Lord, so that it may go well with us.” A beautiful promise—if only they kept it.

f.w: Whether it be good, or whether it be evil
f.g: Whether pleasant or unpleasant to us.

n: God answered after ten days. Even a great prophet had to wait on the Lord’s timing rather than give a quick answer of his own.
Jeremiah gathered Johanan, the commanders, and all the people.
He delivered the answer from the God to whom they had sent him.
If you stay in this land, God will build and plant you—the words of Jeremiah’s call again—because he grieves over the disaster he brought on them.

f.w: will I build you, and not pull you down
I repent me of the evil
f.g: I am grieved over, or relent concerning, the calamity.

n: Don’t fear the king of Babylon—God is with you to save and rescue you from him.

f.w: I am with you to save you

n: God will show you mercy and move Babylon’s king to treat you mercifully and let you stay in your land.

f.w: that he may have mercy upon you

n: But if you say, “We won’t stay here,” disobeying the Lord…
…and insist, “No! We’ll go to Egypt, where there’s no war, no battle trumpet, and no hunger”—Egypt seemed like a safe haven…

f.g: The shofar, sounded as a war alarm.

n: …then hear the Lord: if you are determined to go and settle in Egypt…
…the very sword and famine you fear will catch up with you in Egypt, and you’ll die there. Running from God’s counsel doesn’t outrun trouble.
Everyone determined to go will die by sword, famine, or disease; none will escape.
As God’s anger fell on Jerusalem, it will fall on you in Egypt. You will become a curse and disgrace, and never see this land again.
The Lord’s clear word to the remnant: Do not go to Egypt. Know for certain I have warned you today.
Jeremiah sees through them: you were deceiving yourselves when you asked me to pray and promised to obey whatever God said.

f.g: You were insincere; or, you have put your own lives at risk.

n: I have told you his answer today, but you haven’t obeyed any of it. Asking for revelation while intending to ignore it is a dangerous kind of prayer.

f.w: ye have not obeyed the voice of the LORD your God

n: So know for certain: you will die by sword, famine, and disease in the place where you want to go.
